topics.description: The global colonial and commercial empire developed by the Netherlands, especially during the seventeenth-century Dutch Golden Age.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire’s Periwig Era saw its strong currency deter trade, coining the name for an economic “disease.” The term rangaku referred to books sold by this empire’s traders on the island of Dejima near Nagasaki. This empire’s navy relied on the fluyt and included ships called Sea Beggars. This empire was home to the (*) VOC, the most valuable company of all time. The first stock markets emerged in this empire whose economy experienced a bubble from tulip trading. Land reclamation projects begun in this empire created polders and were drained by now-iconic windmills. For 10 points, name this empire that was centered in Holland.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Dutch Empire [or the Netherlands; or the Dutch Republic; or the United Provinces of the Netherlands; or the United Provinces; or the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands; or the Kingdom of the Netherlands; or Nederlands; accept the Dutch East India Company; accept Dutch Learning; accept Dutch disease; prompt on Holland before mention]

topics.description: A collective historical designation for successive Iranian imperial states, including the Achaemenid, Safavid, and Afsharid realms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander the Great defeated forces from this empire. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this empire, which was ruled for some periods by Achaemenids, Safavids, and Afshars. Rulers of this empire included Cyrus the Great and Xerxes (ZERK-seez) the Great.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The losing forces and Issus and Gaugamela were led by a ruler of this name, though he supposedly fled out of fear at both battles. Another ruler of this name fathered Xerxes the Great, and was Cyrus the Great’s nephew.
parts.answer: Darius [accept Darius III or Darius the Great or Darius I]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Darius the Great, who overthrew Smerdis to become the ruler of Egypt, constructed one of these structures linking the Nile and Red Sea. Another one of these waterways is named for the Egyptian city of Suez.

topics.description: A Japanese warlord and daimyo who unified Japan in the late sixteenth century and launched the invasions of Korea known as the Imjin War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this warlord's death, his son Hideyori (HEE-day-YOR-ee) surrendered power to Tokugawa  Ieyasu (TOH-koo-GAH-wah EE-ay-YAH-soo). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this second “great unifier” of Japan, who launched the Imjin War and succeeded Oda  Nobunaga (OH-dah noh-boo-NAH-gah).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Imjin War consisted of two invasions of this peninsula, whose Joseon (joh-SAHN) navy forced  the Japanese to withdraw from Pyongyang.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hideyoshi also initiated the construction of a gigantic castle in, and named for, this city, where  Hideyoshi's son and wife Yodo-dono (yoh-doh-doh-noh) committed ritual suicide after the Tokugawa  burned the structure down.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Admiral Yi Sun-sin, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Admiral Yi led the navy of Joseon Korea against the invading forces of this Japanese leader, a “Great Unifier” who was succeeded by Tokugawa Ieyasu.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Toyotomi Hideyoshi [accept Hashiba Hideyoshi; accept any underlined part and names in either order]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Admiral Yi invented a type of warship named after this animal, whose deck was covered in hexagonal armor plates and studded with iron spikes.
parts.answer: ANSWER: turtle ship [or gwiseon; or geobukseon]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Admiral Yi’s ships supplemented their cannons with devices known as hwachas which launched these projectiles using rockets. They are more commonly fired from a bow.

topics.description: The sovereign country and constitutional monarchy in Western Europe, established as an independent state in 1830–1831.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a “Free State” with this name, the Force Publique terrorized workers extracting rubber. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Give the name of that colony personally owned by Leopold II. The colony shared this name with two modern-day nations led from Kinshasa and Brazzaville.
parts.answer: Congo [accept Congo Free State or Republic of the Congo or Democratic Republic of the Congo]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Leopold II ruled this European country, whose 1830 independence movement was kicked by a performance of the opera La muette de Portici.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Force Publique cut these body parts off of workers who failed to meet rubber quotas. The workers used these body parts to hold their knives when tapping rubber trees.

topics.description: Theresa May is a British Conservative politician who served as prime minister of the United Kingdom from 2016 to 2019, immediately before Boris Johnson.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a speech where he made car noises, this politician complained about how Daddy Pig holds a negative stereotype. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this politician, who resigned as prime minister of the U.K. in 2022. This politician is often referred to as “BoJo”.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] During the 2019 General Election, Boris Johnson ran on the slogan “Get [this action] done.” This term refers to Britain leaving the European Union in 2020.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This politician, who resigned over Brexit, attacked Johnson and the Partygate scandal in a speech after he announced his resignation. Johnson succeeded this woman as prime minister.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: As mayor of his country's largest city, this politician created a bikeshare program that was nicknamed for him. Sajid Javid resigned from this man's cabinet out of anger at his advisor, Dominic (*) Cummings. In April 2020, this world leader was moved to intensive care after contracting COVID-19. The successor to Theresa May is, for 10 points, what current prime minister of the UK?

topics.description: The ancient Greek city-state that became a major center of classical Greek politics and culture, developed democracy, led the Delian League, and commissioned the Parthenon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city was home to figures like Alcibiades (AAL-sib-ee-AH-deez) and Draco. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this powerful city-state of Ancient Greece. This city organized many other Greek cities into the Delian League after the defeat of the Persian Invasion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Athens is said to be the first polity in the world to have practiced this form of government in which people vote for legislation. However, only wealthy men were actually allowed to participate.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Four Hundred is an example of an Athenian government of this other kind. Especially during wars, Athens often turned to this form of government, whose name is Greek for “rule of the few.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city’s Alcmaeonid family got themselves cursed and exiled until Hippias was overthrown by  Cleisthenes. A harsh law code in this city, which included a death penalty for stealing cabbages, was written  by Draco, and almost entirely replaced by (*) Solon. This city led the Delian League, and embezzled funds from  it to fund the Parthenon. For 10 points, name this birthplace of democracy in Ancient Greece.

topics.description: The surprise Japanese attack on the U.S. Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii on December 7, 1941, which brought the United States into World War II.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The admiral who organized this event was assassinated in the aptly-named Operation Vengeance. This event was known to its perpetrators as Plan Z, and the code phrase "Climb Mount Niitaka" was used to initiate it. Isoroku Yamamoto led this event, which resulted in the (*) sinking of the battleship USS Arizona. For ten points, name this “day which will live in infamy”, a 1941 surprise attack on a Hawaiian naval base.
parts.answer: attack on Pearl Harbor [accept descriptive answers]

topics.description: A 2014 pro-democracy protest movement in Hong Kong whose participants occupied major urban areas and used umbrellas to shield themselves from tear gas.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An event in this city led to the blinding of Indonesian journalist Veby Mega Indah, and was partially inspired by lack of political change following the Umbrella Revolution. Protesters in this city sought the resignation of Carrie Lam. Protests in this city were sparked by a bill that would have allowed (*) extradition to Taiwan and mainland China. For ten points, name this special administrative region of China.
parts.answer: Hong Kong [accept HKSAR or Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China; prompt on People’s Republic of China or Zhongguo or Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Along with an army under the White Banner, armies that used banners of this color were the most prestigious in the Manchu Army. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this color that partially names a Han Dynasty peasant revolt led by the Taoist mystic Zhang Jue [jung jway].

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] A dragon on a yellow field was the flag of this Chinese dynasty. Puyi was the last emperor of this dynasty, which was succeeded by the Republic of China.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In modern times, the color yellow in China has been associated with these objects used by Hong Kong protesters. These namesakes of a 2014 “Movement” have been used to shield protesters from tear gas.
parts.answer: umbrellas [or parasols; accept Yellow Umbrella Movement]

topics.description: The 1845–1852 famine in Ireland caused primarily by potato blight, resulting in mass death, emigration, and major demographic and political changes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Since he believed that this event was divine punishment, aid to victims of this event was reduced by Charles Trevelyan. Victims of this event attempted to escape it by boarding “coffin ships.” This event was partially ended when Robert Peel repealed the (*) Corn Laws. For 10 points, what period of starvation devastated an island off the coast of Britain due to the blight of a namesake staple crop?
parts.answer: Irish Potato Famine [or Great Hunger or Great Famine or Irish Famine]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Choctaw aid during this event is commemorated by the sculpture Kindred Spirits in Midleton.  Charles Trevelyan's (trev-EL-yin's) staunch laissez-faire (LAY-zay FAIR) beliefs limited direct aid  toward victims of this event. Protestant schools engaging in “Souperism” during this event caused  friction with the local population. (*) Coffin ships transported people across the Atlantic away from  this event, which pushed Robert Peele to repeal the Corn Laws. A disease known as “blight” led to, for  10 points, what event that depleted the population of a European island in the 1840s?
parts.answer: Irish Potato Famine [or Great Famine; or Great Hunger; or an Gorta Mór]

topics.description: The Reign of Terror was the period of revolutionary tribunals, mass executions, and political repression during the French Revolution, chiefly from 1793 to 1794, ending with the fall and execution of Maximilien Robespierre.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader used his newspaper, The Defender of the Constitution, to criticize calls for a war against Austria made by Jacques-Pierre Brissot. Cecile Renault attempted to assassinate this leader, who opposed both the Girondists and an atheist cult created by Jacques-René Hebert. This leader promoted the (*) Cult of the Supreme Being and secured power after the death of his former ally Georges Danton. The Thermidorian Reaction began with the execution of this leader and “incorruptible” member of the Committee of Public Safety. For 10 points, name this Jacobin French revolutionary leader who oversaw the Reign of Terror until his own execution by guillotine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This royal’s reputation was destroyed after another woman forged letters in her name to acquire jewelry in the Diamond Necklace Affair. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this last queen of France before the Revolution, who was executed not long after her husband, Louis XVI [sixteenth].
parts.answer: Marie Antoinette (accept Maria Antonia Josepha Johanna)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Upon learning that French peasants were no longer able to afford bread, Marie Antoinette allegedly remarked, “Let them eat” this instead.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Marie Antoinette was killed at the beginning of this bloody period of the French Revolution. This period ended when its leader, Maximilian Robespierre, was also executed.
parts.answer: Reign of Terror (accept The Terror; accept La Terreur)
